entry.title: How I Built an AI-Powered Claw Machine Controlled via WebRTC and Lark/Feishu 🤖🪝
entry.summary:
TL;DR: I built a remotely-operated claw machine robot that anyone on the internet can control in rea``l time. Here's the full story — the hardware, the code, and the breakthrough using OpenClaw.
What if the claw machine was the interface? I wanted to build a real experiment in human-robot interaction (HRI) over the internet — with real-time video and the joyful chaos of a physical claw arm.
Layer Technology
Brain
OpenClaw (AI Agent Framework)
Connectivity
Lark/Feishu Bot API + MQTT
Hardware
Raspberry Pi 4B + Arduino Mega
Video
WebRTC (via Pion)
This is where OpenClaw comes in. Instead of sending raw voltages to servos, I send "intent" to the OpenClaw agent. I added a Lark (Feishu) Skill to the agent. Now, the robot can be controlled directly from a chat group! `javascript To keep the system stable and responsive, I separated the "thinking" from the "moving": Raspberry Pi 4B: The primary gateway. It handles the WebRTC signaling, runs the OpenClaw agent logic, and manages the Lark/Feishu API communication. Arduino Mega: Dedicated solely to PWM signal generation for the 4x high-torque servos. Power Management: A quick pro-tip — Keep your grounds common but your rails separate. I learned this the hard way by frying two Pis before realizing how massive the current spikes from servos can be! Control Latency: Consistent ~45ms over a stable Wi-Fi connection. Video Feed: 1080p @ 30 FPS with sub-200ms latency. Success Rate: ~36.8%. It’s hard enough to be challenging, but fair enough to keep people trying. Cross-Platform: Works seamlessly on modern browsers and as an integrated Lark/Feishu Bot. The entire OpenClaw project is open-source. Whether you want to build your own AI claw machine or use the framework to power a completely different type of robot, I’d love to see what you create. 👉 Check out OpenClaw on GitHub Try the live demo at OpenClaw.ai If you're working on AI agents, IoT, or WebRTC robotics, let's connect in the comments! What would you build with a remote-controlled claw?
